name: Ultraviolet-erasable floating-gate semiconductor memory
summary: A memory chip that could be programmed electrically and wiped clean with ultraviolet light through a window, letting engineers rewrite stored programs during development.
description: A semiconductor floating-gate memory whose cells can be electrically programmed and whose stored charge can be erased by exposing the device through a window to ultraviolet light.

events.statement: Intel advertised 1701/1702 devices as in stock and available for immediate delivery by 27 September 1971.
events.scope: Intel 1701/1702, 2,048-bit ultraviolet-erasable MOS read-only memory, including distributor-programmed versions.
